comments.value: Banning nulls entirely would be even better, but since everything’s based on .NET which made the mistake of including nulls as a side-effect of basically being a 100% ripoff of Java, which made the same mistake, it’s possibly a tricky situation.

details:
This is a data handling paradigm which may help to simplify logic; I have used it quite successfully in my own language projects.  The concept is simple:  Every data value (noodle) could potentially have a value of "null".  This includes nominal value types like int, float, etc.  Every node which takes input(s) checks to see if any of those inputs are null, and acts appropriately.  Most of this time, "acts appropriately" means outputting null for their outputs, but not necessarily.
There are several advantages to this approach:
Being a mostly non-interactive medium (in the sense that there's no terminal to readily display errors on), having a node output nulls is a way of signalling that an error has occurred, without disrupting the execution of the program, particularly in cases where the error is nonfatal. It allows for the easy communication of errors.  Operations which would operate normally without errors, can be bypassed when errors are present, and those errors are propagated on until they are handled.
For example, if you have an array index node, inputs being an array and an index in that array, output being the item at that index, then the output would be null if the input array is null, or the input index is null, or the index is invalid.
The program can then handle this case by checking to see if the output is null; if it is null, it knows that something has gone wrong and can act accordingly.  It generally doesn't care *why* it went wrong, only that it did.
Implementing this also covers several suggestions in this board:

https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/a-is-valid-branch-node (Null Convention essentially implements this)
https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/add-an-optional-parameter-to-custom-event (Null Convention for cases where there isn't a parameter)
https://feedback.vrchat.com/vrchat-udon-closed-alpha-feedback/p/request-add-list-type-handling (Null Convention deals with cases where one attempts to read a list at an invalid index)

Handling these errors takes the form of nodes which do not automatically output nulls when they receive one.  The most basic of these would be the Coalesce operation; the Coalesce operation takes two or more inputs, and returns the first input which is not null.  
Another is a basic IsNull, which returns true if the input is null, or false if it is anything other than null.
title: Null Convention
